## Clear underdogs in every fixture — but a single famous result and the expanded format could keep them alive longer than expected.
[...]
Expectations are tempered by realism. Belgium, Egypt, and Iran are all significantly higher-ranked, and New Zealand will be underdogs in every group fixture. The honest baseline goal is to be competitive, avoid heavy defeats, and chase a famous result.
[...]
The expanded 48-team format means a single shock win — and the right results elsewhere — could keep the All Whites alive longer than expected. Repeating the unbeaten spirit of 2010 would be a triumph; claiming a first-ever World Cup victory (they have never won a World Cup match) would be historic. Anything beyond the group stage would rank among the greatest moments in New Zealand sporting history.
[...]
Darren Bazeley’s New Zealand are pragmatic and disciplined, built to compete against stronger sides. Expect a compact defensive shape — often a 4-4-2, 4-5-1, or 5-4-1 depending on the opponent — that prioritizes organization, deep defending, and minimizing space.
[...]
The game plan typically revolves around frustrating opponents, staying in matches, and exploiting set pieces and direct play to Chris Wood. With Wood’s aerial strength and clinical finishing, crosses and second balls are a genuine route to goal. In midfield, Bell and Stamenic provide the quality to retain possession when chances arise. The All Whites will rarely dominate the ball — their identity is resilience, work rate, and making the most of limited chances, exactly as they did in 2010.
[...]
- The ultimate underdogs — New Zealand are the team everyone loves to see cause an upset.
- Chris Wood — a Premier League striker leading his country one last time at a World Cup.
- The 2010 legacy — can the All Whites recapture their unbeaten magic?
- A first-ever World Cup win — history could be made at any moment.
[...]
Clear underdogs facing a group-stage exit — but a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic dream, and recapturing 2010’s unbeaten magic the fairy-tale ceiling.
[...]
New Zealand are the clear underdogs of Group G and will struggle against Belgium, Egypt, and Iran on paper. The most likely outcome is a group-stage exit. But the All Whites’ organization and Chris Wood’s quality make them dangerous in a one-off match, and the expanded format means a single famous result could keep their hopes flickering. A first-ever World Cup win — perhaps against Egypt or Iran — is the realistic dream. Recapturing the unbeaten spirit of 2010 would be the fairy-tale ceiling.
